## `conc_read_write_lock` Exclusion

**Why excluded**: The program contains only class definitions (`ReadWriteLock`, `ProtectedDict`). The auto-discovery heuristic in `_load_entry_fn()` searches for top-level functions named `sort`, `search`, `run`, `main`, etc. None exist in this program.

**Impact on evaluation**:
- 58 of 744 test pairs (7.8%) involve this program
- All 58 pairs receive `similarity = 0.5` (neutral imputation on genome=None)
- Maximum AUROC bias: ±0.02 (estimated from fraction of affected pairs)
- Direction of bias: toward 0.5 (compressed toward noise floor)

**Pre-registered status**: The failure of class-based programs to yield genomes was anticipated. These programs test behavior through class instantiation, not direct function calls — a known limitation of the V2 auto-discovery approach.

**Disclosure**: All 58 affected pairs are identifiable via `base_id.startswith("conc_read_write_lock")`.

## Q&A (Preregistered Questions)

**Q1: Is execution-derived SBG stable?**  
Yes — for 12/13 programs, features are completely deterministic (CV=0.0). `conc_read_write_lock` cannot be measured via auto-discovery.

**Q2: Is observed SP/SC separation larger than noise?**  
Per-type analysis is required (see SP_TYPE_ANALYSIS.md). At the aggregate level, AUROC=0.528 is within the random-label noise floor CI [0.461, 0.544]. Per-type signal is above noise for SC-11, SC-12, SC-8, SC-1, SC-6.

**Q3: Which dimensions are noisy?**  
No dimensions are noisy (CV=0.0 for all measured programs).

**Q4: Are any programs pathological?**  
`conc_read_write_lock` is functionally excluded (class-based architecture incompatible with auto-discovery). All other programs are stable.

## Comparison with Phase 3A

In Phase 3A, noise floor was measured for 1/10 programs (9 FILE_NOT_FOUND using wrong program names). Phase 3B corrected this by using the actual 13 benchmark programs. The results are:
- 12/13 programs: same as api_rate_limiter (CV=0.0 — completely deterministic)
- 1/13 program: excluded by design (class-based)
- No programs are noisy in the traditional sense
